body.x: CEA forecasts record industry revenue for 2015, with 4K Ultra-High Definition televisions, unmanned systems, wearables and other emerging technologies driving growth

The keynote speeches by Ford and Intel for CES 2015 were given on the opening day of the CES. More than 3,600 exhibitors launched new products on this day, and the leaders of Ford and Intel making major announcements and outlining their vision of technology innovation.

On Tuesday, Gary Shapiro, president and CEO, started off with the announcement that revenues for the consumer electronics industry are projected to grow three percent in 2015 to reach an all-time high of $223.2 billion according to the semi-annual industry report compiled by CEA. He also reinforced the importance of a forward strategic path on innovation both for the industry and the world.

Mark Fields, president and CEO of Ford Motors, introduced Ford’s new Smart Mobility plan, which promises to solve today’s global transportation challenges with its open source providing a better customer experience, more flexible user-ship models and social collaboration. And with a mission to "make the first Ford autonomous vehicle accessible to the masses and truly enhancing customers’ lives," he announced that Ford is currently testing Fusion Hybrid, a fully autonomous car that uses existing technology from Ford’s semi-autonomous cars and includes LiDAR sensors to sense objects and advanced algorithms to help predict vehicle and pedestrian traffic.

Intel Corporation CEO Brian Krzanich said that 2015 will mark the next technology consumer wave, the movement from a two-dimensional world to a three-dimensional world in his keynote address. Krzanich introduced Intel innovations such as Real Sense (depth interpreter), True Key (password eliminator), and the Curie wearable (sports activity identifier). In line with touting its capabilities, HP’s Dion Weisler, executive vice president of Printing & Personal Systems, appeared on stage to announce HP’s multi-jet fusion 3D printing powered by Intel’s processing. Oakley CEO Colin Baden showed numerous live demonstrations with Real Sense technology jacket and avoiding obstacles in “game of drones.” Krzanich concluded by discussing the importance of diversity and inclusion in technology, and announcing Intel’s creation of the Technology and Diversity Initiative.

Some 20,000 products will launch at the 2015 CES from major global brands to a record number of 375 tech startups in the Eureka Park Marketplace. Innovative products and technologies range from the latest in wearables, unmanned systems, health and fitness tech, robotics, 3D printing, sensor technologies and beyond.

Owned and produced by the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA), the 2015 CES is the world’s gathering place for all who thrive on the business of consumer technologies and runs Jan. 6-9 in Las Vegas.
